keywords: Dirt / soil / grime terra, terrae f.; sordēs, sordium f. pl. terra, terrae f. — dirt as earth or soil; the ordinary material dug out of a trench. sordēs, sordium f. pl. — dirt as grime or filth. A singular also exists; the plural is the useful everyday form given here. Terram hūc fer. — Bring the dirt here. Sordēs ē manibus terge. — Wipe the dirt off your hands. latin: māchina, māchinae f.; compāgēs, compāgis f.
keywords: Scaffold / scaffolding / framework māchina, māchinae f.; compāgēs, compāgis f.  māchina, māchinae f. — scaffold / scaffolding for building. This is an explicit ancient sense in Lewis & Short I.B.3, citing Digest 13.6.5 and Pliny 19.2.8 §30; the noun is broader than modern English “machine.” Morgan–Owens also lists it under scaffolding. compāgēs, compāgis f. — framework / joined structure; Morgan–Owens lists this too for scaffolding. The relevant structure is identified by context. māchina ex fistulīs ferreīs — scaffolding made of iron tubes; our descriptive phrase for the modern construction-site object. Operārius in māchinā stat. — The worker is standing on the scaffold. Māchinam iuxtā domum cōnstruunt. — They are assembling the scaffolding beside the house. These sentences are composed. pēgma, pēgmatis n. is another ancient framework/machinery noun, especially for theatrical stage machinery and board fixtures. Its ancient examples do not by themselves establish the modern tube-and-clamp construction sense; māchina has the clearer explicit builder’s-scaffold entry. keywords: Scaffold pole / upright / crossbar / diagonal brace fistula ferrea; ferrum trānsversum; fulcīmentum oblīquum  fistula, fistulae f.; fistula ferrea — tube; iron tube. Our application to a hollow scaffold pole. For a wooden pole or beam, asser, asseris m. is ancient; the shape and material determine which noun fits. fistula ad perpendiculum posita — upright / vertical tube, literally a tube placed plumb; our description, not a verified modern component headword. latin: tabulātum, tabulātī n.; tabula, tabulae f.
keywords: Scaffold platform / deck / plank / guardrails / base plate / ladder tabulātum, tabulātī n.; tabula, tabulae f.  tabulātum, tabulātī n. — planked flooring, floor or platform; applied here to the scaffold’s working deck. The floor/storey sense also appears in the existing house-layout entry. tabula, tabulae f. — plank / board; an individual wooden plank of the deck. A metal deck is a modern application of the platform vocabulary, not evidence that ancient platforms used the same fittings. repāgula, repāgulōrum n. pl. — bars / barriers, ancient especially for door bars; our functional extension to guardrails. ferrum trānsversum ad marginem tabulātī positum describes one metal rail placed at the edge of the deck. Neither is asserted to be a standardized modern scaffold-component term. lāmina, lāminae f. — plate / sheet. lāmina sub fistulā posita — base plate under a scaffold tube; our description, not a verified technical compound. scālae, scālārum f. pl. — ladder / stairs; gradus, gradūs m. — step or ladder rung.
